items.question: How are reading and speaking durations calculated?
items.answer: Silent reading speed is computed at 238 words per minute (standard collegiate benchmark), while conversational speaking time is calculated at 150 words per minute.

items.question: What is keyword density and how does the stop-word filter work?
items.answer: Keyword density measures the percentage frequency of a word relative to total text words. Enabling the stop-word filter excludes common functional words (such as "the", "and", "is") to reveal primary topical keywords.

items.question: How are compound emojis and accented characters counted?
items.answer: Characters are evaluated using Intl.Segmenter grapheme clusters so that multi-codepoint emojis (like 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦) and combining accent sequences count accurately as single characters.

items.question: Are hyphen-joined words counted as one word or two?
items.answer: Hyphenated words (such as "well-known") are counted as a single word token, matching standard Microsoft Word and Google Docs conventions.

items.question: Can this tool handle entire novels or essays over 100,000 words?
items.answer: Yes. Text segmentation runs via optimized native Web APIs in linear O(n) time, analyzing large manuscripts within milliseconds without browser freezing.

items.question: How are sentence boundaries identified?
items.answer: Sentence segmentation relies on international linguistic rules via Intl.Segmenter, treating abbreviations and introductory interjections (< 3 words) with proper contextual grouping.

items.question: Why do character tallies differ when whitespace is excluded?
items.answer: The total character metric tallies every grapheme cluster including space characters, tabs, and line returns. The characters without spaces metric strips all Unicode whitespace codepoints to reflect printable prose density.

items.question: Is my unpublished writing safe from cloud logging?
items.answer: Completely safe. The entire counting engine runs strictly within your browser sandbox. No text is ever uploaded to a server, logged, or indexed.
